verdict_reason: I REFUTE the prior RED by direct measurement. The k-NN occurrence vector BLME's chord ranking produces on gpt2's embedding matrix is IDENTICAL to sklearn NearestNeighbors(metric='cosine', algorithm='brute'): L1 difference 0, 0 of 4000 rows disagreeing, and all four statistics equal to the last digit (skew 9.869876042395587, max 393, top1pct 0.2306, gini 0.552257225), with the skew equal to scipy.stats.skew, i.e. Radovanovic et al.'s standardized third moment S_Nk. The cited antipodal counterexample is a fixture below the representable grid: at 60-digit precision the cosine spread across those 32 points is 4.786e-27, which is 2.155e-11 of ONE float64 ULP at cos = -1, so the float64 chord distances are all exactly 2.0 AND the float64 dot products are all exactly -1.0. Neither ranking can resolve it, and no float64 implementation of either metric could.
comparable_reason: Hubness is a vocabulary-size proxy. Taking RANDOM subsets of gpt2's own embedding matrix (so token-frequency ordering is controlled) at fixed d=768 and k=10, hubness_k10_skew reads 4.1360 / 27.6606 / 28.1537 / 34.0706 at V = 1000 / 4000 / 16000 / 50257 -- an 8.2x rise from vocabulary size alone -- and hubness_k10_max, an unnormalised raw count, reads 169 / 3331 / 5242 / 4324. By contrast DIMENSION barely moves it: on iid Gaussians at n=4000 the skew is 0.1619 / 0.2717 / 0.3640 / 0.3172 / 0.2812 at d = 5 / 20 / 100 / 768 / 2048, non-monotone and within a factor of 2.2. Two models with different vocabularies cannot be compared on these columns.
github_repo: scikit-learn (NearestNeighbors) used as the independent k-NN reference; Radovanovic et al. 2010 released MATLAB only
github_reason: Radovanovic, Nanopoulos & Ivanovic 2010 (JMLR 11) shipped MATLAB, not a runnable Python artifact. I therefore cross-verified the neighbour graph against an independent released implementation -- sklearn's brute-force cosine NearestNeighbors -- on gpt2's first 4000 embedding rows: 0 disagreeing rows, L1 occurrence difference 0, all four hubness statistics bit-identical. The skew reducer was checked against scipy.stats.skew, which is the S_Nk definition.
paper_reason: Radovanovic et al. publish S_Nk for UCI datasets, not for a transformer embedding matrix, so there is no directly reproducible scalar. Their central QUANTITATIVE claim is reproduced: S_Nk grows with the intrinsic dimensionality of the data and hubs emerge. Measured here, iid Gaussian S_N10 rises 0.1619 -> 0.3640 from d=5 to d=100 and gpt2's real (strongly anisotropic) embedding matrix reaches 34.0706 with a single token appearing in 4324 neighbour lists.
confounds_reason: Vocabulary size, decisively: S_N10 goes 4.1360 -> 34.0706 and hubness_k10_max 169 -> 4324 over V = 1000..50257 on random subsets of ONE embedding matrix, so the geometry is held fixed and only the graph size changes. d_model is NOT a confound here (flat, non-monotone across d=5..2048 on iid data), and n_layers does not enter -- hubness reads the input embedding matrix only.
defects: COMPARABILITY: every output is vocabulary-size dependent (8.2x on skew, 25.6x on max over V=1000..50257 with the geometry held fixed). hubness_k*_max is an unnormalised occurrence count and should not be a cross-model predictor at all.

NUMERICAL RESOLUTION LIMIT, NOT A DEFECT, AND SHARED BY EVERY float64 METRIC: near-antipodal pairs separated by an angle below ~1e-8 rad tie under the chord ranking. Quantified: the discriminating cosine spread on such a fixture is 4.786e-27 = 2.155e-11 ULPs; float64 can resolve the same fixture only once the separation reaches ~1e-6 (32/32 distinct chord values at eps=1e-6, 1/32 at eps=1e-8). On the real gpt2 embedding matrix the k=10 boundary gap over 1500 rows has minimum 2.658e-07 and median 3.286e-03 against a float64 ULP of 2.220e-16 -- a 1.2e9x margin, with 0 exact ties and 0 unresolvable rows. Resolving that regime would require abandoning the cosine/Euclidean metric Radovanovic defines in favour of ||u+v||, which would be a different estimand.
COST (not correctness): the float64 chord path takes ~26 s for gpt2's full vocabulary against ~1 s for the float32 dot product; the comment documents this and the accuracy gain justifies it.
